original_question: Does every non-Kähler compact complex surface admit a birational structure?
target_in_paper: Question 44 in §10.2: "Does any non-Kähler compact complex surface admit a birational structure?" This is the nearest official formulation of the draft in arXiv:2312.03907. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft already matches the paper's official problem almost verbatim: it has the same universal quantifier, the same class of objects (non-Kähler compact complex surfaces), and the same existence question about a birational structure. The only substantive omission is that "birational structure" is a technical term defined immediately beforehand. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
missing_details: "Birational structure" should be defined explicitly: the surface must admit a holomorphic atlas whose transition maps are restrictions of birational self-maps of projective space; in the surface case this means birational self-maps of P^2_C. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should say that a "compact complex surface" is a compact complex manifold of complex dimension 2 over C. The paper states the definition in the category of complex manifolds and the problem specializes it to surfaces. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

The paper places the question inside the subsection on compact complex manifolds arising from generalized Hénon maps, but the question itself is not restricted to Hénon-associated surfaces; that surrounding discussion is motivation, not part of the formal statement. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

A nearby contextual remark is that the problem "reduces to the case of VII0 surfaces"; this is useful paper-faithful context, but it is not part of the official formulation and should not replace it in the refined question. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
refined_question: For every non-Kähler compact complex surface X, i.e. every compact complex manifold of complex dimension 2 over C that is not Kähler, does X admit a birational structure in the following sense: there exists a holomorphic atlas {(U_i, phi_i)} such that each phi_i maps U_i biholomorphically onto an open subset of C^2, and for every nonempty overlap U_i ∩ U_j, the transition map phi_j o phi_i^{-1} is the restriction of a birational self-map of P^2_C? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
justification: The draft is already essentially exact. In the PDF of arXiv:2312.03907, the matching official statement is Question 44 in §10.2. The indispensable sharpening needed to make it fully stand-alone is to spell out the paper's definition of "birational structure" and to make explicit that the ambient objects are compact complex surfaces, i.e. complex dimension 2 over C. The remarks immediately after Question 44 add context—namely that the problem reduces to class VII0 surfaces and that certain deformations S with b_2(S) <= 3 are known to admit birational structures—but those remarks are not part of the official question itself. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
